summary: Ponytail commits an agentic harness (benchmarks/agentic/run.py with judge, completeness and compare scripts) and results with per-task medians, 95% bootstrap intervals and sign tests: on 39 tasks with 5 runs per task and arm (585 sessions), Ponytail 5 reports -53% lines of code, -45% output tokens, -26% cost and -41% time versus no skill, and a test for 98% of risky logic (no skill: 68%). The same results report where it did not come out ahead: hidden checks are level (87/90 vs 86/90 for no skill, and all three arms passed 30 of 30 security runs), no-skill tests catch more injected bugs where a test exists (77% vs 69%), and a blind judge leaned toward the no-skill replies (82 : 106, p=0.09, not significant). An earlier single-shot benchmark found ponytail 26.2% and 38.7% more expensive than no skill on gpt-5.4-mini and gpt-5.5. Raw run workspaces are not committed, so checking the results requires a paid live rerun, and the /ponytail-review detection rates (100% vs 87% for no skill) appear in an image caption without data.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
